:::{#exr-loglik-iid}
#### Log-likelihood of an independent sample

For mutually independent data $\dsn{X}$,
use @thm-lik-iid
to write the [log-likelihood](#def-loglik) $\ell(\theta)$
as a sum over the observations.
What does each term become
if the $X_i$ also share a common distribution $\p(X = x \mid \theta)$?
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-loglik-iid}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\ell(\theta)
&\eqdef \log{\Lik(\theta)}
&& \text{(definition of log-likelihood)}\\
&= \log{\prodin \p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(likelihood of an independent sample)}\\
&= \sumin \log{\p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta)}
&& \text{(log of a product is a sum of logs)}
\end{aligned}
$$

With a common distribution, $\p(X_i = x_i \mid \theta) = \p(X = x_i \mid \theta)$,
so each term is $\log{\p(X = x_i \mid \theta)}$.

:::
